newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds plod ahead, spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds plod ahead, spreads widen.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities recorded modest gains on Friday, with yield spreads widening a touch to Treasuries, traders said.

Pass-throughs were propelled on Treasuries' heels after a volatile durable goods orders report showed most of the 4.6 percent gain in September was due to civilian aircraft orders, a Midwest trader said.
"But mortgage spreads versus Treasuries widened out slightly," the trader added, noting a lack of active trading in pass-throughs.
By late Friday, current coupons were 4/32 higher.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 4/32 at 99-17/32, yielding 109 basis points over Treasuries.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were up 4/32 as well, at 99-14/32 and 99-20/32, respectively. The 10-year Treasury note climbed 8/32, yielding 6.54 percent.
Another trader said many eyes are waiting for the results of the November Presidential elections.
"The focus is on the election right now," he said, adding the market would suffer if voters don't reelect Clinton and a Republican Congress.
